full_judgment: 3. Defendant no.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia that the suit is not maintainable, barred by limitation, bad for defect of parties. Further contending that defendant purchased the suit land from plaintiffs at a consideration of taka 20,000/00 vide registered kabala dated 04.03.1982 for the purpose of establishing a private graveyard; Being cheated by the cunning plaintiffs, defendant no.1 got the deed executed and registered in the form of Waqf deed; Being simple and naive, defendant no.1 could not understand ulterior motive of the plaintiffs; After purchase, defendant no.1 filled up ditches and established a family graveyard in 12 decimals of land and planted trees in other part; Defendant no.1 gifted 11 decimals of land to the school belonged to defendant no.3 vide registered deed dated 18.01.2001 and delivered possession thereof within knowledge of the plaintiffs and all other concerns; Suit land is not enrolled as Waqf property in the office of Waqf Administrator; Suit is liable to be dismissed.
